cls: Nicotinic cholinergic receptor agonist (smoking cessation aid)
pharm: Nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) agonist at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors; relieves craving and withdrawal during smoking cessation.
quick: 2 or 4 mg lozenge/gum per dose; or patch 7-21 mg/24h, tapered
Avoid food/drink 15 min before and during oral NRT
Avoid; quit without NRT preferred - weigh risk/benefit
Nicotine passes into milk; weigh against smoking
summary: Nicotine, supplied as replacement therapy (gum, lozenge, patch, inhaler, nasal spray), reduces craving and withdrawal symptoms to aid smoking cessation. Oral and transdermal forms are dosed by smoking intensity and tapered over about 12 weeks. Nicotine itself is the addictive component of tobacco; NRT delivers it more slowly and at lower peaks to support quitting. Caution is needed in recent cardiovascular events, pregnancy, and breastfeeding.
indications: Aid to smoking cessation - reduces nicotine withdrawal symptoms including craving
As part of a behavioral support/cessation program

dosage.c: Lozenge - first cigarette within 30 min of waking
dosage.n: Use at least 9 lozenges/day in first 6 weeks; max 5 in 6 h, 20/day

dosage.c: Lozenge - first cigarette after 30 min of waking
dosage.n: Dissolve slowly 20-30 min; do not chew or swallow

dosage.c: Gum - first cigarette after 30 min of waking
dosage.n: Heavier smokers use 4 mg; chew-and-park technique

dosage.d: Start 21 mg/24h x6 wk, then 14 mg/24h x2 wk, then 7 mg/24h x2 wk
dosage.n: Lighter smokers may start at 14 mg/24h

admin: Lozenge: place in mouth and let dissolve slowly over 20-30 minutes; minimize swallowing; do not chew or swallow whole; move from side to side
Gum: use chew-and-park technique (chew until tingle, park against cheek, repeat ~30 min)
Do not eat or drink 15 minutes before or while using oral NRT (acidic beverages reduce absorption)
Patch: apply to clean, dry, hairless skin; rotate sites; remove before MRI
Stop smoking completely on the quit day before starting
moa: Nicotine binds and stimulates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the CNS and autonomic ganglia, producing the pharmacologic effects (and dopaminergic reward) that maintain tobacco dependence. Replacement therapy substitutes a controlled, lower-peak dose to relieve craving and withdrawal, allowing gradual tapering.
preg: Pregnant smokers should be encouraged to quit without medication first; nicotine may harm the fetus. Use NRT in pregnancy only if the likelihood of quitting with its help outweighs the risk of continued smoking plus residual NRT nicotine.
lact: Nicotine passes into breast milk. Weigh the lower, intermittent exposure from NRT against the harms of continued smoking; intermittent forms timed after feeds are generally preferred over continuous patches if used.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment; use caution in severe renal impairment.
hepatic: Nicotine is largely hepatically metabolized; use caution in severe hepatic impairment.

moderate: Smoking cessation alters metabolism of CYP1A2 substrates (theophylline, clozapine, olanzapine) - levels rise as smoking stops, may need dose review
minor: Insulin - smoking cessation may improve insulin absorption/requirements
interactions.food: Avoid acidic foods and beverages (coffee, soda, juice) 15 minutes before and during oral NRT use.
interactions.diagnostics: Remove transdermal patch before MRI to avoid burns.

monitoring: Smoking cessation progress and craving/withdrawal symptoms
Cardiovascular status and blood pressure in at-risk patients
Signs of nicotine excess (nausea, palpitations, dizziness) - indicates over-dosing or continued smoking
counsel: Stop smoking completely when you start - using nicotine while still smoking can cause overdose symptoms
Let the lozenge dissolve slowly or use the chew-and-park technique for gum; do not eat or drink 15 min before/during
Follow the tapering schedule over about 12 weeks
Nicotine is addictive; use only as directed and combine with behavioral support
Keep all forms away from children and pets - even used patches/gum can be toxic
pk: Buccal absorption within minutes; patch over hours
Oral ~1-2 h; patch sustained over 16-24 h
Store at room temperature; keep away from children and pets
pearls: Nicotine is the addictive component of tobacco; NRT delivers it at lower peaks to ease quitting
Match dose to smoking intensity (time to first cigarette and cigarettes/day)
Combining a patch (baseline) with gum/lozenge (breakthrough craving) improves quit rates
Acidic drinks reduce buccal absorption - avoid before/during oral NRT
Stopping smoking increases serum levels of CYP1A2 substrates (clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline)
missed: If you miss a dose of oral NRT, use it when you feel a craving. For the patch, apply a new one as soon as you remember and resume the daily schedule; remove the old patch.
overdose: Nicotine overdose causes nausea, vomiting, salivation, abdominal pain, sweating, headache, dizziness, hearing/vision disturbance, weakness, tachycardia then bradycardia/hypotension, and at high doses convulsions and respiratory failure. Remove the source (patch), provide supportive care, manage seizures and cardiorespiratory support; activated charcoal may help. Pediatric ingestion can be fatal - seek emergency care.
